title: LDA internal helpers take pre-encoded y_encoded plus n_classes and must not recompute uniques
answers: LDA means_/priors_ order mismatch with classes_
body:
Invariant: in sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py, `_class_means(X, y_encoded, *, n_classes)` and `_class_cov(X, y_encoded, priors, ..., *, n_classes)` take integer codes that index `self.classes_`. The same goes for `LinearDiscriminantAnalysis._solve_lstsq`, `_solve_eigen` and `_solve_svd`. Row `i` of `means_` and `priors_[i]` belong to code `i`.
The helpers loop over `range(n_classes)` with `y_encoded == idx`. The numpy path uses `np.bincount(y_encoded, minlength=n_classes)` and `np.add.at`. They must not call `unique`/`unique_inverse` on y again. That extra pass was the redundant work this change removed, and raw labels can be strings or live on another device.
n_classes comes from `self.classes_.shape[0]`. `fit` sets `classes_` and computes priors via `xp.unique_counts(y_encoded)` before it dispatches to a solver, so any new solver or helper must keep that order and pass `y_encoded`, never the raw `y`.
